findings.text: Starting with an empty WaitGroup, Go increments the counter before starting f. If f calls Go on the same group before finishing, the child is counted before the parent can be removed. On a normal return or runtime.Goexit, f's deferred calls run before the wrapper calls Done. The last decrement to zero releases every registered waiter. runtime.Goexit ends the task goroutine and allows the group to complete.

findings.text: Starting with an empty WaitGroup, if Add(1) completes before Wait reads the state, Wait registers and blocks if Done has yet to occur. If Done takes the counter back to zero first, Wait returns immediately. If Wait instead reads zero before Add(1), that Wait returns without waiting for the subsequently registered task. For work that this Wait is meant to cover, the contract requires the positive Add from zero to precede Wait.

Starting with a zero counter outside synctest, an unmatched Done executes Add(-1). Add stores the decrement atomically before checking the resulting counter, then panics with "sync: negative WaitGroup counter". If the caller recovers, the same WaitGroup still has a counter of -1. With no intervening changes, a subsequent Add(1) brings it to zero and a subsequent Wait returns immediately.

Starting with one outstanding task and a registered waiter, the final Done takes the counter to zero, clears the packed state, and releases the waiter. If a new Add(1) lands after that clear and the old waiter reads the new nonzero state after acquiring the semaphore, the old Wait panics. If the old waiter reads zero first, a new Add after that read can escape this check even if Wait has yet to return. The reuse contract requires every previous Wait to have returned.

Starting with a Go task as the last outstanding task and a waiter already blocked, if f panics and the panic escapes f and its deferred calls, the wrapper recovers the panic value and immediately panics again before reaching Done. The task stays counted and the waiter stays blocked pending process termination from the uncaught panic. The Go contract explicitly excludes a panicking f.

findings.text: Starting with an unused WaitGroup inside a synctest bubble, Add(1) associates the group with that bubble. If Wait registers before the final Done, Done clears the state and disassociates the group before releasing the waiter. If Done reaches zero with no registered waiters, it returns with the bubble flag still set. A subsequent zero-counter Wait can clear the flag and association. Until that cleanup occurs, an Add from outside the bubble encounters the retained flag and terminates with a fatal error even though the previous task count reached zero.
findings.question: OPEN: Is the comment requiring all Add calls to come from the same bubble meant to apply only until the current association is cleared, and is a zero-counter Wait intended to be required before crossing the bubble boundary when the last Done had no waiters?
